original_test_intent: Verify on the intended platform's BIOS Setup boot-order page that the installed operating system is represented by the project-approved unique UEFI boot option name, rather than an ambiguous generic device label or an entry belonging to another disk/OS installation.
original_method: Select the unique row; record SUT, BIOS build, installed OS/version, boot disk and expected UEFI option label; obtain a maintenance window and console path; restart or enter Setup only through the approved procedure; navigate without changing values to the boot-order screen; correlate the displayed label with the intended boot device and capture the full ordered list; exit without saving; verify the approved OS still boots and preserve any discrepancy.
manual_activity: A qualified operator enters BIOS Setup, reads and captures the complete boot-order page, correlates the approved unique OS label to the intended boot device, exits without saving and verifies recovery.
required_inputs: Installed OS distribution/version and boot disk/EFI-system-partition identity
Canonical expected UEFI Boot#### label and its device/path mapping, including allowed normalization
Approved BMC KVM/local console path, maintenance authorization, entry/exit procedure and recovery owner
safety_requirements: Confirm the correct SUT and known-good console before any restart or Setup entry
Use view-only navigation and capture the entire relevant boot-order context
Do not reorder, create/delete entries, alter Secure Boot/storage/security settings or save changes
Exit using the approved no-save path and prove normal boot afterward
Stop on wrong target, missing/ambiguous entry, accidental change, boot failure or lost console; do not repeatedly reboot
agent_execution_scope: Organize supplied SUT/OS/UEFI identity and operator screen evidence
Compare the captured label and device/path with the approved expectation
Record ordering and ambiguity without altering firmware state
Do not infer the BIOS entry from Linux text alone, control an unapproved reboot, edit NVRAM or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve the canonical label, exact UEFI option/device-path mapping and allowed capitalization/version normalization
Approve console/maintenance/restart and no-save recovery procedure
Review the captured BIOS evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: No shell command can prove the source-required BIOS Setup label. DeepSeek correctly leaves it to an operator, but BIOS/KVM context and the exact expected UEFI entry still need definition.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Qualified operator uses the approved console to open BIOS Setup, displays the complete boot order, captures the target entry and exits without saving; optional OS-side `efibootmgr -v` may corroborate only, not replace the BIOS screen.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Interactive BIOS Setup, boot-order unique-name check, ubuntu 22.04 example and 10/10-minute estimate remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Predefine the canonical UEFI option and device path, capture the full BIOS boot-order screen plus target mapping, use a no-save exit and verify the same OS resumes boot.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact target identity, entry/device correlation, console/maintenance safety, whole-list evidence and post-exit boot verification.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: The running OS name or an `efibootmgr` entry cannot demonstrate how this BIOS Setup implementation actually renders and orders the boot-device label.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Entering Setup can interrupt service, and accidental edits or save operations can change boot behavior even though the intended observation is read-only.

project_override_considerations: If validated BMC KVM automation can deterministically render and capture the BIOS page, it may assist navigation, but a human still owns the interactive screen observation and no-save recovery under the current source. The ubuntu label is an example, not authority for every image.
expected_evidence: SUT/BIOS/OS/boot-disk identity and approved UEFI entry/device-path mapping
Timestamped full BIOS boot-order screenshot/video or console capture showing the exact label and position
Post-exit expected-OS boot evidence, recovery events and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require a unique OS label in BIOS boot order. The example is illustrative; project data must supply the actual expected string.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The visual BIOS observation is clear and executable by a qualified operator. Expected label, console and maintenance are ordinary prerequisites, so MANUAL ONLY is appropriate rather than BLOCKED.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2232 Wistron-BMC Sanity-00014-V001: approve the SUT/BIOS build, installed OS/version and boot-disk/EFI identity; canonical UEFI boot-option label, Boot####/device-path mapping and allowed normalization; full boot-order expectation; approved KVM/local-console Setup entry/no-save exit, maintenance authorization, post-boot oracle and recovery procedure.

review_improvement: Preserves the required BIOS screen judgment while preventing an OS-side proxy, ambiguous label or accidental firmware edit from being accepted as coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: The property under test is the firmware UI's rendered boot option, not merely the OS release or NVRAM data visible after boot. An entry can have the right-looking label while pointing to the wrong device path, or the correct disk can be displayed generically; both label and device identity matter. Because observing the page requires interrupting normal boot and navigating an interactive firmware UI, the case is manual and service-affecting even though no setting should change. A full-screen capture and no-save recovery are necessary evidence.
